_meta.about: Topic -> design decisions for the namokposter skill. Keys starting with '_' are not topics. See topic-guide.md.

solemn.about: Copy that mourns or remembers the dead is set soberly whatever else it mentions: when one of these words is in the headline, label, sub-headline or paragraph, only the type themes listed here are chosen (best first).

_meta.palette_rule: ink/bg >= 7:1 and accent/bg >= 3.5:1 (WCAG relative luminance); every topic has light and dark grounds
_meta.engine_note: Engines of the planned styles are an assumption (material looks = Blender, graphic and painted looks = three.js); the trios were balanced on it. Re-check against each style.json.
_meta.matching: Match Korean keywords as substrings and English ones on word boundaries, case-insensitively (acronyms such as AI, UX, DJ, IR, LoL case-sensitively). Where keywords overlap, count only the longest ('푸드 페스티벌' is food, not also music). Weight title and eyebrow about 3x the body. 'general' keywords are stop-words. Keep the top one or two topics; a season is usually a second topic that sets the palette.
_meta.ko_not_inside_note: A keyword does not count where it is only part of one of these longer words (the trio is not a Christmas tree).
_meta.ko_whole_word_note: One-syllable Korean words are left out of the keyword lists because they match inside other words (봄 in 돌봄). Count them only when they stand alone as a whole word after stripping particles (은/는/이/가/을/를/의/에/과/와/도/로).
_meta.month_note: Korean seasons by month. A date alone is weak evidence: use it to break ties between palettes of the main topic, not to make the poster 'about' the season.

retro.composition: Name the decade and stay in it: each era has its own type (deco caps, 60s grotesque, 70s fat serif, 80s signboard gothic, Y2K chrome) and its own two or three inks. Korean 뉴트로 rests on square-frame Hangul lettering in the signboard tradition, revived since Kim Kijo's 2008 lettering for 장기하와 얼굴들; a solid drop shadow, a label on a block, print grain.
avoid: rays radiating from a sun disc — the commonest retro motif and the one that reads as the Rising Sun flag; use arches, wavy stripes, checkerboards, stars

craft.composition: Craft fairs show material before message: the poster looks made of the thing — clay, thread, wood, paper — photographed or rendered plainly, in natural-dye colours, with quiet type (a humanist sans, a book serif, or one handwritten line).
